title: Robot Research for Trunk Rehabilitation and Assessment
summary: Robotic mechanisms, control methods, and human-subject experiments for trunk function recovery and quantitative assessment.
image_alt: Robot system for trunk rehabilitation and assessment
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China, Young Scientists Fund (C)
overview: This project investigates high-compatibility variable-stiffness design and dynamic compliant control for trunk rehabilitation robots. It builds on prior work in wearable robotic braces, serial–parallel mechanisms, and robot-assisted trunk assessment.
challenge: A trunk rehabilitation robot must provide adequate support across changing postures and impairment levels while remaining comfortable, safe, and mechanically compatible with human motion.
approach: The project combines variable-stiffness mechanism design, dynamic compliant control, biomechanical modeling, and experimental evaluation with rehabilitation users.

title: Modular Upper-Limb Rehabilitation Robot
summary: Modular and reconfigurable robot design for different upper-limb training tasks and individual rehabilitation needs.
overview: This research addresses individualized rehabilitation needs after upper-limb impairment through modular and reconfigurable robot systems that adapt to different joints, training movements, and stages of recovery.
challenge: Patients differ in movement capacity, target joints, and rehabilitation goals. Fixed robot configurations often struggle to combine broad adaptability, rapid reconfiguration, and safe training.
approach: The work combines modular mechanism design, configuration reassembly, kinematic analysis, robot control, and prototype experiments to support multiple upper-limb training tasks.

title: Robot Research for Neck Rehabilitation and Assessment
summary: Multi-degree-of-freedom rehabilitation robots and control methods for neck function recovery and objective assessment.
image_alt: Serial-parallel robot system for neck rehabilitation and assessment
overview: This research develops a multi-degree-of-freedom robot system for guided neck motion, rehabilitation assistance, and quantitative functional assessment.
challenge: Neck motion is spatially complex and safety-critical. The robot must guide movement accurately, accommodate individual differences, and collect meaningful motion and interaction data for assessment.
approach: The work integrates serial-parallel mechanism design, kinematic and dynamic analysis, compliant control, and experimental evaluation for combined neck rehabilitation and functional assessment.

title: Abnormal Sitting Posture Recognition and Monitoring Across Subjects
summary: Flexible pressure sensing and cross-subject recognition improve the generalization of abnormal sitting posture monitoring across individual differences, supporting broader deployment for adolescent posture monitoring.
image_alt: Experiment for abnormal sitting posture recognition and monitoring using flexible pressure sensing

title: Key Robotic Technologies for Active Rehabilitation of Lumbar Disc Herniation
summary: Robot design, control, and evaluation methods for active rehabilitation of lumbar disc herniation.
image_alt: Abstract graphic for the lumbar rehabilitation robot project
overview: This project develops key robotic technologies for active rehabilitation of lumbar disc herniation, connecting compliant physical assistance with measurable rehabilitation training.
challenge: Lumbar rehabilitation requires assistance that supports training goals without imposing rigid motion or excessive physical load on the user.
approach: Research activities span wearable mechanism design, assistance control, biomechanical measurement, and prototype evaluation.

title: Key Technologies for Rehabilitation Robots Based on Rigid–Flexible Coupled Actuation
summary: A high-compatibility lumbar rehabilitation robot using rigid–flexible coupled actuation and variable stiffness.
image_alt: Abstract graphic for the variable-stiffness lumbar robot project
overview: The project explores rigid–flexible coupled actuation for a high-compatibility, variable-stiffness lumbar rehabilitation robot.
challenge: Wearable lumbar systems need to balance support capacity, stiffness range, compact structure, and compatibility with complex torso motion.
approach: The work integrates variable-stiffness actuation, compact mechanism optimization, compliant control, and experimental characterization.
